text.p: Fund manager Amvesco Plc said on Wednesday it was comfortable with key performance targets after reporting strong first quarter results, which included figures for AIM Management Group for the first time.

It reported pre-tax profits of 29.7 million pounds ($48.6 million) in the quarter to end-March from 15.3 million a year earlier, and said AIM, which was only included in results from the beginning of March, contributed 9.8 million.

Amvesco chief financial officer Robert McCullough told Reuters in an interview that he was not targeting full year earnings but was comfortable with the group's key target of a 35 percent operating margin by the end of the year.
"Obviously a lot depends upon what happens to the markets in the future but we feel at this point in time that 35 percent is not only a good target but a target that we feel comfortable with."
The group came in with an operating margin of 34.8 percent from 27.4 percent at the end of 1996 on the back of improvements in both the Invesco business and the inclusion of AIM results.
The merger between Invesco and AIM was completed at the end of February.
Revenues in the first quarter were 84.8 million sterling against 55 million in the same 1996 period. AIM accounted for 22.1 million sterling of the first quarter 1997 revenue.

Funds under management at the combined operation stood at $160 billion at the end of March, up $65.5 billion from the end of 1996. The rise was mostly accounted for by the inclusion of AIM funds totalling $64.7 billion.
McCullough said uncertainty about what it would do with a $425 million credit facility it took out last year made forecasting full year earnings difficult.

"We still have got a bit of work to do. Looking at what we can do from a cash management perspective and also what we can do to lower the tax rate are two activities that we are aggressively pursuing, but really with 45 days under our belt have not had a chance to adequately deal with it."
But he said the business was flowing very well from a cashflow perspective, and Amvesco was looking closely at how much and how quickly it could return some of the money of the credit facility.

McCullough said the group saw a further $700 million in funds under management move out of its U.S. institutional business in the first quarter, bringing the total to around $1.5 billion over six months as investors moved to higher yield investments.

But he said the overall figure for funds under management in the U.S. institutional business was stable over the quarter as market gains made up for the loss of the accounts. It had also picked up some new small accounts which it hoped would compensate for the lost business over time.
The group had no plans to change its investment philosophy, which is core equity, or mostly large cap stocks.

"As large institutions continue to look at the huge uplift in the market they are continuing to re-evaluate how much they want to keep in the core equity and bring it out to more aggressive investment styles," he said.
"We have debated over whether we should be changing our investment style and concluded that what served us well for 25 years is what we need to continue working with."
The company will change its name to Amvescap Plc following shareholder approval on May 8 after a legal challenge to the name Amvesco in the U.S.
